主要内容: The Walt Disney Company appointed Thomas O. Staggs as its new Chief Operating Officer, effective February 4, 2015. The appointment was formalized through the 'Staggs Agreement,' signed on February 5, 2015. Mr. Staggs will receive an annual salary of $2,000,000, starting from February 4, 2015, with the potential for annual salary increases not less than $2,000,000. He is also eligible for an annual performance-based bonus, with a target bonus of not less than 250% of his annual base salary. The agreement includes equity-based long-term incentive plans, under which Mr. Staggs will be granted a long-term incentive award with a target accounting value of four times his annual base salary for each fiscal year during the term of the Agreement. The awards are subject to performance and market conditions, and the actual compensation may vary based on these factors. The agreement also includes provisions for termination for cause or good reason and outlines the structure of the awards, including stock options and performance-based restricted stock units. The text emphasizes that the awards do not guarantee a minimum amount of compensation and are subject to the Compensation Committee's discretion. The Walt Disney Company made changes to its employment agreements in early 2015. On February 4, 2015, the company amended the Employment Agreement with Alan N. Braverman, extending his employment as Senior Executive Vice President, General Counsel, and Secretary from March 31, 2016, to March 31, 2018. His minimum salary was also set at $1,500,000. Additionally, the company filed an Employment Agreement with Thomas O. Staggs as Exhibit 10.1. These amendments were part of the company's ongoing efforts to manage its leadership structure and ensure continued executive stability. The changes were documented in the company's filings and signed by Roger J. Patterson, the Associate General Counsel and Assistant Secretary, on February 5, 2015. The text outlines the conditions under which Mr. Staggs may terminate his employment with 'good reason,' including a material reduction in duties, relocation beyond 50 miles from the greater Los Angeles area, or a material breach of the Agreement. In such cases, Mr. Staggs is entitled to termination benefits, including a lump sum payment of base salary, a pro-rated bonus, and the vesting of unvested stock options and restricted stock units. The Agreement also allows for the extended exercisability of stock options and requires Mr. Staggs to execute a release and provide consulting services for six months following termination. The text emphasizes the Company’s obligation to waive performance conditions on restricted stock units unless necessary for tax deductibility.
